description:
Redwood Inference will build an internal “Unit Economics” dashboard to make inference cost drivers visible and actionable across product, engineering, and finance. The primary output metric is blended $/1M output tokens, with drilldowns by (1) model (and model version / quantization profile), (2) region, and (3) customer tier (self-serve / dedicated / private / enterprise). The dashboard is intended to support Cost Optimization Automation efforts (batching, caching, quantization profiles) by (a) quantifying impact, (b) identifying regressions, and (c) enabling prioritization of runtime/infra work.

Goals:
- Provide a trusted, finance-aligned definition of “blended $/1M output tokens” that reconciles with infra spend inputs and platform metering.
- Enable drilldowns and comparisons (time range, model, region, customer tier) for identifying unit-cost outliers.
- Surface contributing signals: cache hit rate, batching efficiency, average output length, streaming vs non-streaming, and quantization profile.
- Establish data quality checks, SLOs, and an on-call playbook so the metric is dependable for exec reporting.

Scope:
- Data model + definitions (token attribution, customer tier mapping, region normalization, model identifiers, quantization profiles).
- Telemetry pipeline changes (output token metering parity across streaming paths, cost attribution inputs, aggregation jobs, warehouse views).
- Console backend APIs for dashboard queries and drilldowns.
- Initial Console UI (internal-only) with filters, time series, and top-N tables.
- Operationalization: alerts on missing data / drift, runbooks, and incident response procedures.

Non-goals (v1):
- External customer-facing cost dashboards (possible future follow-on).
- Fully automated optimization actions; this project provides measurement and diagnostics that feed automation.

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Aditya Rao (Optimize) for requirements and prioritization.
- Engineering (Console & Tooling): Dylan Brooks (Dir Eng), Chloe Martin (EM) for dashboard/API implementation.
- Engineering (Telemetry & Analytics): Logan Wright (EM), Nadia Rahman (Staff) for metering, aggregation, and data quality.
- Finance: Laura Bennett (CFO), Rishi Malhotra (FP&A) for methodology alignment and KPI reporting.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant for SLOs, alerting, and operational readiness.

Proposed timeline (10–12 weeks):
- Weeks 1–2: kickoff, metric definitions, data model, gap analysis (streaming parity, dimension mapping).
- Weeks 3–6: telemetry + aggregation implementation; first warehouse views; initial API contract.
- Weeks 5–8: Console UI + backend endpoints; iteration with finance/product; early internal dogfood.
- Weeks 8–10: data quality hardening, SLO/alerts, runbooks, and access controls.
- Weeks 10–12: staged rollout to Finance/Product/Eng, exec readout, backlog for v1.1 (additional drilldowns, quality signals, automation hooks).
